title: European Sector Atlas — Relationship-First Sector Map
purpose: Fill the World and North Programme layers with the productive, infrastructural, social and dependency sectors that sit between states and the European Economic Graph. This is an ontology and research scaffold, not a claim that every sector has already been fully measured.
method: Use NACE-compatible sector families where possible, then extend them with cross-cutting systems such as finance, infrastructure, data and strategic dependencies. A sector is treated as a network of inputs, firms, workers, infrastructure, regulation, finance, trade and outputs.

sector_families.name: Agriculture, Forestry & Fisheries
sector_families.research: Map land, farm structure, input suppliers, processing, cold chains, ports, subsidies, labour and food-security dependencies.

sector_families.name: Food Processing & Distribution
sector_families.research: Map processing concentration, cold storage, wholesalers, retailers, packaging, imports and bottlenecks.

sector_families.name: Mining & Raw Materials
sector_families.research: Map extraction, refining, processing, recycling and foreign-source concentration for critical materials.

sector_families.name: Chemicals & Petrochemicals
sector_families.research: Map feedstocks, plants, cross-border pipelines, energy intensity and downstream industrial dependencies.

sector_families.name: Pharmaceuticals & Biotechnology
sector_families.research: Map API dependencies, manufacturing sites, research institutions, procurement and critical medicines.

sector_families.name: Metals, Machinery & Industrial Equipment
sector_families.research: Map machine builders, component suppliers, industrial clusters and imported high-value inputs.

sector_families.name: Automotive & Mobility Manufacturing
sector_families.research: Map OEMs, Tier-1/Tier-2 suppliers, battery chains, plants, logistics and technology dependencies.

sector_families.name: Aerospace & Defence
sector_families.research: Map industrial capacity, public procurement, supply chains, research institutions and external dependencies.

sector_families.name: Construction & Built Environment
sector_families.research: Map construction capacity, building stock, renovation rates, materials and public/private investment.

sector_families.name: Energy Generation
sector_families.research: Map generation by technology, ownership, capacity factors, fuel exposure, costs and grid constraints.

sector_families.name: Energy Networks & Storage
sector_families.research: Map interconnectors, transmission bottlenecks, distribution networks, storage and digital control systems.

sector_families.name: Oil, Gas & Fuels
sector_families.research: Map import origins, terminals, pipelines, refineries, storage, contracts and substitution options.

sector_families.name: Nuclear Energy & Fuel Cycle
sector_families.research: Map reactors, ownership, fuel supply, engineering capability, waste systems and new-build pipelines.

sector_families.name: Transport & Logistics
sector_families.research: Map ports, rail freight, roads, airports, shipping, logistics firms, corridors and bottlenecks.

sector_families.name: Maritime, Ports & Shipbuilding
sector_families.research: Map North Sea/North Atlantic ports, shipyards, shipping ownership, repair capacity and critical sea lanes.

sector_families.name: Aviation & Airports
sector_families.research: Map airports, airline concentration, aircraft supply chains, fuel and regional connectivity.

sector_families.name: Water, Wastewater & Water Resilience
sector_families.research: Map abstraction, treatment, leakage, industrial use, agriculture and drought exposure.

sector_families.name: Waste, Recycling & Circularity
sector_families.research: Map material flows, recycling capacity, export of waste, repair systems and secondary-material demand.

sector_families.name: Telecommunications & Connectivity
sector_families.research: Map operators, fibre, mobile networks, subsea cables, satellite systems and equipment dependencies.

sector_families.name: Semiconductors & Electronics
sector_families.research: Map design, fabrication, packaging, equipment, materials, foundries and external dependencies.

sector_families.name: Cloud, Data Centres & Compute
sector_families.research: Map data centres, operators, power demand, fibre, cooling, sovereignty and AI compute capacity.

sector_families.name: Software, AI & Digital Services
sector_families.research: Map major platforms, open source, public digital infrastructure, AI capacity and dependency on non-European stacks.

sector_families.name: Banking, Finance & Capital Markets
sector_families.research: Map banks, insurers, funds, payment systems, sovereign debt holders and capital-market links.

sector_families.name: Insurance & Pensions
sector_families.research: Map pension assets, insurers, public/private schemes and their investment relationships.

sector_families.name: Healthcare & Care Economy
sector_families.research: Map hospitals, primary care, medicines, workforce, procurement, ageing and public/private financing.

sector_families.name: Education, Skills & Training
sector_families.research: Map education spending, skill shortages, vocational systems, universities and regional human-capital concentration.

sector_families.name: Research, Science & Innovation
sector_families.research: Map research institutions, funding flows, patents, industrial partnerships and technology-transfer pathways.

sector_families.name: Public Administration & Government Services
sector_families.research: Map competences, agencies, staffing, procurement, transfers, duplication and service outcomes.

sector_families.name: Retail, Hospitality & Consumer Services
sector_families.research: Map distribution concentration, imports, logistics, labour and household demand.

sector_families.name: Media, Culture & Information
sector_families.research: Map ownership, platforms, archives, information flows and concentration of public attention.

sector_families.name: Tourism & Visitor Economy
sector_families.research: Map regional dependence, infrastructure pressure, ownership and seasonal labour.

sector_families.name: Labour, Demography & Migration
sector_families.research: Map participation, ageing, migration, vacancies, skills and regional mismatch.

sector_families.name: Housing & Real Estate
sector_families.research: Map housing stock, rents, ownership, construction capacity, mortgages and affordability.

sector_families.name: Security, Defence & Resilience
sector_families.research: Map procurement, industrial capacity, stockpiles, critical infrastructure and alliance dependencies.

high_value_blind_spots: industrial water use and water-energy coupling
maintenance and repair capacity rather than new investment alone
subsea cable ownership and repair fleets
pharmaceutical active ingredients and critical medicines
pension and insurance ownership of infrastructure and corporate debt
public procurement as a demand-side industrial policy
skilled trades and technical workforce bottlenecks
food cold chains and processing concentration
ports as coupled energy, trade, defence and industrial nodes
housing as both social infrastructure and financial asset
data centres as coupled electricity-water-network infrastructure
research institutions as upstream nodes in industrial value chains

source_basis.finding: EU value added in 2025 was 73.5% services, 19.2% industry, 5.5% construction and 1.8% agriculture/forestry/fishing.

EU strategic-dependency monitoring identifies sensitive product dependencies including raw materials, batteries, active pharmaceutical ingredients, hydrogen, semiconductors and cloud/edge technologies.

source_basis.source: European Commission Critical Raw Materials Act
source_basis.finding: Strategic raw-material policy links extraction, processing, recycling and diversification to industrial resilience.
Semiconductors, cloud, AI, open source and energy digitalisation are being treated as interconnected technological-capacity systems.
Housing and food together account for 72% of the EU material footprint in the analysed 2021 data, making them major hidden resource-system nodes.
Water abstraction can be traced across electricity cooling, agriculture, manufacturing, construction, mining and public water supply.
Energy-price shocks propagate through agriculture, distribution, transport and then broader production and services, illustrating sector coupling.
